creator: Alexander Terp
description:
amterp, Chat Notes 2026-10-05: "temporary hide or archive", and 2026-10-07: "headless muster agents ie No visible pane but can bring forward". Confirmed 2026-10-07: "I was kind of imagining like a right click where you can hide a pane, and it goes into like a hidden menu where you can then later bring them back if you want to." And: "I guess the hidden is kind of the same as headless, right?"

So: right-click a pane -> Hide. The pane leaves its tab and its agent keeps running. A Hidden list (menu or sidebar section) shows hidden panes with their states and brings one back. The CLI gets the same: `muster pane hide`, `muster pane show`, and `muster pane new --hidden` for a pane made hidden from the start, which is the headless agent.

Open design questions: where a shown pane goes (its old tab and place, the current tab, a new tab); whether a hidden pane still notifies (see the quiet-pane card (a_2die7W9ru)); what `muster window` prints for it (today `(hidden)` means a pane in a tab not on screen, a different thing); and whether the daemon can hold a pane in no tab at all, which the laptop-gone card (a_2die7Kz7l) also wants.

The bigger shape this is stage 1 of is the sub-agents card (a_2die894mw).
title: 🫥 Hide a pane from a right-click, and bring it back from a Hidden list
